'''Andrey A. Varlamov''' (born 25 April 1954) is an Italian [[Condensed matter physics|condensed matter physicist]] of Ukrainian origin, who works on [[superconductivity]], fluctuation phenomena, [[graphene]] physics, and [[thermoelectricity]].
He is a [[principal investigator]] at the Institute of Superconductors, Oxides and Other Innovative Materials and Devices ([[SPIN-CNR]]) in [[Rome]], Italy.

==Early life and education==
Andrey Varlamov was born on 25 April 1954 in [[Kyiv]], [[Ukraine]]. In 1971 he graduated from [[Kyiv Natural Science Lyceum No. 145]]. The same year, he was admitted to the [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]] and got his master's degree [[cum laude]] from the [[Landau Institute for Theoretical Physics|Landau Institute]] six years later. Immediately after, he started the Ph.D. program under the supervision of [[Alexei Alexeyevich Abrikosov|A.A. Abrikosov]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/abrikosov-alexei.pdf|author=M. R. Norman|title=Aleksei A. Abrikosov|publisher=National Academy of Sciences|year=2018}}</ref> at the [[National University of Science and Technology MISIS|Moscow Institute of Steel and Alloys]] and received his Ph.D. in [[condensed matter]] [[physics]] in 1980. At the same university he was awarded his Habilitatus (Doctor of physical and mathematical sciences) in 1988.<ref name=bitp>{{cite web|url=http://bitp.kiev.ua/en/doctors/varlamov|title=Andrey Varlamov|publisher=Bogolyubov Institute for Theoretical Physics|accessdate=12 January 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==
{{BLP sources section|date=March 2025}}
From 1981 to 1999 he worked as a researcher, senior researcher (1985), associated (1987) and full professor (1990) at the Department of Theoretical Physics in [[National University of Science and Technology MISIS|Moscow Institute of Steel and Alloys]]. In 1993 he became an invited fellow at the Condensed Matter Theory Group of [[Argonne National Laboratory]] in United States and then starting from 1996 worked as an invited professor at first at the University of Rome Tor Vergata and then from 1997 to 2000 held the same position at both [[University of Bordeaux]] and the [[University of Florence]]. From 1999 to 2005 he was a visiting professor at the [[University of Minnesota]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pld.uniroma2.it/members/varlamov_curriculum.html|title=Andrey Varlamov (AV)|publisher=Pulsed Laser Research Group|accessdate=12 January 2019}}</ref> and the [[University of Pavia|Pavia]]. At the [[University of Rome Tor Vergata]] he is an adjunct professor to this day. Since 1999 he works as a research director at the Institute of Superconductors, Oxides and other Innovative Materials and Devices of the Italian National Research Council ([[SPIN-CNR]]).<ref name=bitp/>

In 2018 Andrey Varlamov and [[Andreas Glatz]] had written a what became known as the ''Perfect Pizza'' equation.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.livescience.com/64016-physics-of-perfect-pizza.html|title=Italian Physicists Wrote a 'Perfect Pizza' Equation, Because Not All Heroes Wear Capes|author=Brandon Specktor|date=6 November 2018|accessdate=12 January 2019}}</ref>

==Honorable titles==
In 2009 he was elected as correspondent member of the [[Istituto Lombardo Accademia di Scienze e Lettere]] Brera.
In 2011 he was awarded the degree of ''Doctor of Honoris Causa'' at the Bogolyubov Institute for Theoretical Physics.
<ref name=bitp/>
In 2014 he was honored with the degree of  ''Doctor of Honoris Causa'' at the [[Mediterranean Institute of Fundamental Physics]].
Since 1985 he is a member of the Editorial Board (1986-1992 vice-editor-in-chief) of the popular scientific journal for students ''[[Kvant (magazine)|Kvant]]'' of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bpias.eu/15-october-2014-physics-in-the-kitchen-by-prof-andrey-varlamov/|title=Physics in the kitchen by Andrey Varlamov, Ph.D|date=15 October 2014|accessdate=12 January 2019}}</ref>
